properties.decision:
RE-OPENED 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word, after storyflow gap D arrived and the same defect reproduced in this design within the hour.

WHAT WAS DECIDED BEFORE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH NOW. dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling (ACCEPTED, 2026-07-24) met a legitimate island, tried three bridges, refused all of them as lies, accepted the island, and concluded: "flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DETECTOR RATHER THAN IN THE DESIGN." That fix was never built. The decision records why — the specific island DISSOLVED on its own when cap:session-memory turned out to belong to both cmp:docs and cmp:temporal, giving documentation a real tie rather than a manufactured one. So the disposition became moot and the general principle it stated was left unimplemented. The old decision is NOT wrong and is NOT being un-accepted (dec:reopen-supersedes); what is re-opened is the clause it deferred.

WHAT CHANGED, and it is two independent measurements on the same day. (1) storyflow's governance model is a 121-node cluster tripping `disconnected_community` with `generate_bridge` proposed — a remedy that would fabricate traceability between fleet-operations governance and product design, which are two genuinely separate concerns sharing a repo. (2) THIS DESIGN reproduced it at 5 nodes: capturing governance requirements under dec:governance-integrates-not-splits produced heal:33d1548dae64e97a with the same suggested fix, and no honest bridge existed.

⭐ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: both clusters are GOVERNANCE, and both GROW as governance is captured properly. dec:governance-integrates-not-splits has just committed this project to exactly that growth. So the detector currently penalises the work the project decided to do, and gets louder the better the work goes.

⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT BOTH PROJECTS ARRIVED AT INDEPENDENTLY, SIXTEEN DAYS APART — this is the strongest evidence available that the shape is right, and it is also the trap. The 2026-07-24 decision: "the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection." storyflow, 2026-08-09: "a real disconnection would arrive inside a 121-node warning everybody has already learned to ignore." Same sentence, two authors, neither aware of the other.

THE OPTIONS.
(A) A DECLARED PARTITION — a marker on a Project or Component saying this subtree is deliberately separate, so the detector reports "N declared partitions, 0 undeclared". Same shape as `granularity`'s opaque-vs-pending_expansion and as `enforced`'s tri-state, which is the argument for it: reflow2 has twice decided that a CHOICE and an UNFINISHED STATE must not look identical, and this is the third instance. COUNTER: a marker is exactly the kind of thing that gets set once and never revisited, and dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches warns in its own text that "another marker nothing reads" would be a fourth instance of the very disease.
(B) TEACH THE DETECTOR THE CATEGORY, as the 2026-07-24 decision assumed — infer that a cluster of purely-governance or purely-documentation nodes has no operational coupling by nature, the way dec:operational-spof already excludes non-operating things from SPOF findings. CHEAPER for the user, no new vocabulary. COUNTER: an inference cannot be argued with, and a genuine governance island would be hidden by the same rule that exempts the legitimate one.
(C) FIX ONLY THE SUGGESTED REMEDY — leave the finding, drop `generate_bridge` where no honest edge exists, and say so. THE SMALLEST HONEST STEP, and it removes the part storyflow called corrupting. COUNTER: it leaves the permanent un-clearable warning, which is the half that makes people stop reading.
(D) ACCEPT ISLAND BY ISLAND, as today. COUNTER: an acknowledgement is a one-time answer to a finding whose size keeps changing — acknowledged at 88 it now reads 121, and nothing says when it became a different finding.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. The requirement req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate states the need; this node holds the unmade choice about its shape, and (A) is written first only because it is what both reporters proposed, not because it is recommended.
properties.name: DECIDED — stop proposing fabrication now; declare partitions next, and only if something reads the declaration back
properties.rationale: SETTLED 2026-08-09 by Anthony: "agree with: C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D." The four options and their counter-arguments are preserved above rather than pruned, so a later reader can see what was weighed and not merely what won. The read-back condition is not decoration: it is what stops option A becoming the fourth instance of the disease `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches` documents, and it is written into `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` as an acceptance test rather than left as an intention.
